roadmap.scope: ADO Bug #6306, Jira on-prem (Data Center / Server) Releases only. The additional-fields re-sync is split to Story #6307 and is out of scope. All code is in /storage/repos/Lighthouse/Lighthouse.Backend (JiraWorkTrackingConnector, JiraReleaseVersionReader, tests). No UI change.
roadmap.goal: On Jira Data Center / Server the Release picker, the Release refresh and the forecast publish all call rest/api/3 routes (and rest/api/3/project/search) that DC does not serve, so the picker silently comes back empty. Make the release capabilities deployment-aware (Cloud keeps its exact routes; DataCenter and Unknown use the v2 routes DC serves, with DC's bare-array project list and no server-side status filter), make a missing route loud, stop pinning a transient Unknown deployment, and then guard structurally so no Jira capability can be added again without its DC answer: one routes object per deployment, a source-scan test that allows rest/api/ literals only there, and a shared fake DC Jira the release capabilities are tested against.
roadmap.paradigm_note: C# / NUnit 4 in Lighthouse.Backend.Tests. There is no DISTILL wave for a bugfix: RED is a crafter-authored regression test through the driving port (IDeliverySourceProvider.GetOptions / ResolveMany and IDeliveryForecastPublisher.PublishAsync on JiraWorkTrackingConnector, against an HTTP stub answering like Jira DC), which must fail on today's code for the bug's reason before production code changes.

validation.reviewer: orchestrator (inline, following the bug-6054 / bug-6254 precedent for a surgical bugfix)
validation.notes: No architect dispatch: the Phase-1 RCA (nw-troubleshooter, 2026-10-15, docs/feature/bug-6306-jira-onprem-releases/rca.md, approved by the maintainer) prescribes every fix site. Orchestrator verified: the three rest/api/3 release literals (JiraWorkTrackingConnector.cs:2935, :2969, :3251); JiraDeployment enum + DeploymentCache + GetDeploymentType (:34, :90, :2761-2803, Unknown cached at :2779); JiraStub answers serverInfo as Cloud (JiraDeliverySourceProviderTest.cs:1028); publisher test pins v3 (JiraDeliveryForecastPublisherTest.cs:106); JiraConnectorTestSetup offers only ATeamOnJiraCloud (:119); rest/api literals outside the connector exist only in JiraReadException.cs message strings (:69, :79, :86).

user_decisions: Maintainer approved the RCA and the fix direction (2026-10-15).
Maintainer approved the three-layer recurrence guard: routes object per deployment (separate refactor commit after the fix is green), source-scan test, shared fake DC Jira.
Start now, without waiting for the reporter's serverInfo / status codes (asked in parallel).
Document the minimum supported Jira Data Center / Server version as 8.x and later.
out_of_scope: Re-syncing teams/portfolios when a connection's additional fields change (Story #6307).
Surfacing 'some Releases could not be read' in the UI (needs a sketch; possible follow-up).
Live verification against a real DC instance (none available; reporter asked for serverInfo + status codes).

phases.name: Release capabilities work on Jira Data Center
phases.description: Regression tests through the driving ports against a DC-shaped Jira fake, failing on today's code, then the minimal deployment-aware fix.

steps.name: The Release picker lists a DC instance's unreleased Releases
steps.description: GetOptions for jira-release against a Jira that answers like Data Center returns that instance's unreleased, unarchived Releases instead of an empty list. A shared fake DC Jira is introduced as a test helper.
steps.scenario_name: On a Data Center Jira the Release picker offers each project's unreleased Releases
red_to_green_tests: JiraDeliverySourceProviderTest :: GetOptions on a Data Center Jira offers the unreleased Releases of every project
JiraDeliverySourceProviderTest :: GetOptions on a Data Center Jira leaves out released and archived Releases even though the route cannot filter by status
JiraDeliverySourceProviderTest :: GetOptions on a Data Center Jira pages through a project's versions
JiraReleaseVersionReaderTest (or the existing reader test file) :: the DC project list (a bare JSON array) is read; a page whose root is not an object reads as empty-and-last instead of throwing
criteria: A shared test helper FakeJiraDataCenter (an HttpMessageHandler, or whatever shape the existing JiraStub uses so the connector can be pointed at it the same way) answers rest/api/2/serverInfo with deploymentType "Server"; answers 404 to EVERY rest/api/3/* route and to rest/api/2/project/search; serves GET rest/api/2/project as a bare JSON array of {id,key,name}; serves GET rest/api/2/project/{key}/version as the paged envelope {startAt,maxResults,total,isLast,values:[...]} with version objects {id (string),name,archived,released,releaseDate?,projectId} and IGNORES any status query parameter; serves GET/PUT rest/api/2/version/{id} and records writes. It is built from the DC REST docs cited in rca.md, not from Cloud payloads.
RED: GetOptions on a DC connection returns an empty list on today's code (the rest/api/3/project/search call 404s) - captured before production code changes.

GREEN: the release sweep resolves the deployment once (GetDeploymentType) and passes it to ReadVisibleProjects / ReadReleasesOf. Cloud keeps byte-identical routes: rest/api/3/project/search?startAt&maxResults and rest/api/3/project/{key}/version?startAt&maxResults&status=. DataCenter uses rest/api/2/project (one call, bare array) and rest/api/2/project/{key}/version?startAt&maxResults (no status). Unknown tries rest/api/2/project/search (paged, Cloud v2) and on 404 falls back to rest/api/2/project; versions use the v2 route without status.

Where the route could not filter by status, the picker keeps a version only if it is neither released nor archived (the same set Cloud's status= filter returns for the picker). Refresh asks for every status and needs no filter.
JiraReleaseVersionReader gains a reader for the bare-array project list, and ReadPage answers an empty last page for a non-object root instead of throwing InvalidOperationException.
A non-success answer to the project list is logged at Warning, naming the route and the deployment; per-project version-read failures stay at Information (a 403 on one project is expected).
All existing Cloud tests in JiraDeliverySourceProviderTest stay green unchanged.
dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test with the standard live-connector exclusion filter green.
steps.implementation_notes: Pre-apply docs/ci-learnings.md. No comments citing the bug number or internal ids; the commit body carries the why. Prefer [TestCase] over duplicated tests. Commit: fix(jira): the Release picker reads a Data Center Jira's projects and versions (bug 6306)

steps.name: Release refresh and forecast publish work on DC; Unknown is not pinned
steps.description: ResolveMany (refresh) and PublishAsync use DC routes on a DC Jira; a failed serverInfo is no longer cached as Unknown for the life of the process.
steps.scenario_name: On a Data Center Jira a bound Release refreshes and the forecast publishes to it
red_to_green_tests: JiraDeliverySourceProviderTest :: ResolveMany on a Data Center Jira resolves a bound Release (date and carried work) instead of reporting it unreadable
JiraDeliveryForecastPublisherTest :: PublishAsync on a Data Center Jira reads and writes rest/api/2/version/{id}
JiraDeliveryForecastPublisherTest :: PublishAsync on Cloud still writes rest/api/3/version/{id} (the existing :106 assertion, now explicitly the Cloud case)
a test (in the connector's deployment-detection tests, or the provider test) :: when serverInfo fails once and then answers, the second call routes by the answered deployment (Unknown is not cached)
criteria: RED: the DC refresh and DC publish tests fail on the 01-01 code for the bug's reason (rest/api/3/version 404 / no Release resolved), captured before the production change.
PublishAsync resolves the deployment and uses rest/api/3/version/{id} on Cloud, rest/api/2/version/{id} on DataCenter and Unknown, for both the GET and the PUT of its read-merge-write.
ResolveMany on DC finds the bound Release through the 01-01 sweep and its carried-work search (already DC-safe through rest/api/latest/search) still runs.
GetDeploymentType no longer stores Unknown in DeploymentCache; Cloud and DataCenter answers are still cached.
JiraConnectorTestSetup gains ATeamOnJiraDataCenter (or the equivalent DC connection builder) next to ATeamOnJiraCloud if the tests need it.
Existing Cloud tests stay green; dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test (standard exclusion filter) green.
steps.implementation_notes: Commit: fix(jira): refresh and publish a Data Center Jira's Releases, and ask again after a failed deployment check (bug 6306)

phases.name: No Jira capability can forget Data Center again
phases.description: Structural recurrence guard, after the fix is green: routes per deployment, a literal-scan test, the docs.

steps.name: One routes object per Jira deployment owns every REST route
steps.description: Refactor: an abstract JiraRestRoutes with Cloud and DataCenter implementations, one abstract member per capability, chosen by JiraDeployment; every rest/api literal in the connector moves into it. Behaviour unchanged.
steps.scenario_name: Refactor only: every existing Jira connector test stays green against both Cloud and the DC fake
red_to_green_tests: No new behaviour. The full Jira unit/acceptance test set (standard exclusion filter) is the safety net and must stay green at every micro-step.
criteria: JiraRestRoutes is an abstract class (or sealed hierarchy) with exactly two concrete deployments, Cloud and DataCenter, plus a way to get the routes for a JiraDeployment (Unknown maps to the DataCenter/v2 routes, with the Unknown project-list fallback from 01-01 preserved). Every capability is an abstract member, so adding a capability does not compile until both deployments answer it. Shape/parameter differences live beside the route (e.g. whether the project list is paged, whether versions can be filtered by status).

Every rest/api/... literal in JiraWorkTrackingConnector.cs (search incl. rest/api/3/search/jql and rest/api/latest/search, issue PUT, status, field, filter, changelog, issueLinkType, myself, serverInfo, project list, project versions, version) is replaced by a JiraRestRoutes member. Where a route is the same on both deployments it is defined once in the base class (still inside JiraRestRoutes.cs).
JiraReadException messages take the route text from JiraRestRoutes (or are reworded) so no rest/api literal remains there.
No behaviour change: Cloud requests are byte-identical to before (assert via the existing tests that pin URLs).
dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test (standard exclusion filter) green. The orchestrator will run the JiraIntegration category deliberately after this step as the live Cloud check.
steps.implementation_notes: Pure refactor commit, separate from the fix commits. Commit: refactor(jira): one routes object per Jira deployment owns every REST route

steps.name: A test refuses rest/api literals outside the routes object; the DC floor is documented
steps.description: An NUnit source-scan test under Architecture/ fails if any rest/api/ literal appears in backend production code outside JiraRestRoutes.cs. ci-learnings gains the rule; jira.md names the minimum supported DC/Server version.
steps.scenario_name: A Jira REST route written outside the routes object fails the build's tests
red_to_green_tests: JiraRouteLiteralsTest :: no production .cs file other than JiraRestRoutes.cs contains a "rest/api/" literal
JiraRouteLiteralsTest :: the scan itself finds a planted literal (guards against a scan that reads no files, e.g. a wrong root path)
criteria: Follow the style of the existing source-scan tests in Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Architecture (e.g. SecretReadPathSourceStructureTest.cs) for locating the production source root.
The scan asserts it read a non-trivial number of files and that JiraRestRoutes.cs itself contains literals, so a broken path cannot pass vacuously.
RED evidence: temporarily reintroduce a literal (or point the scan at the pre-02-01 connector text) and capture the failure; then GREEN on the real tree.

docs/ci-learnings.md gains one rule in the ledger's existing format: any new Jira REST call goes through JiraRestRoutes and names its Data Center route and response shape; rest/api/3 and rest/api/2/project/search are Cloud-only.
docs/concepts/worktrackingsystems/jira.md states Jira Data Center / Server 8.x or later is supported, in the doc's existing voice and using the configurable terminology defaults.
dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test (standard exclusion filter) green.
steps.implementation_notes: Commit: test(jira): a REST route written outside the routes object fails the architecture tests (bug 6306). Docs may be a separate docs(jira) commit.
